correctness.rationale: The proof uses the precisely stated classical inversion reciprocity and the upper bound of Chen–Dunn–Hewett–Silas Proposition 2.6 on interior residues. For small a, exact L_b(a)-T factorization is (a-3)(b+1)(b+1-3a)/(12a). For large multipliers, reversal reduces to a strictly positive concave N_b(c), and middle multipliers reduce to a strictly positive concave P_b(a); endpoint factorizations were checked symbolically. The exceptional a=(b+1)/2 is the inverse of 2. Independent exact recurrence enumeration of all 498 odd moduli b=7..1001 confirms the inequality and complete equality conditions; symbolic inequalities, not the finite sweep, prove all b.

value.rationale: Settles the explicit odd-modulus n=3 case of a numbered published open inversion-ordering conjecture. The exact sharpness/equality classification is a nontrivial all-modulus theorem requiring reciprocity plus a new global three-region comparison.

final_claim: For every odd b>=7 the third distinct smallest inversion number of a multiplication permutation modulo b is at least (b+1)(b-2)/6, with equality iff b=2 mod3, attained only by multipliers 3 and (b+1)/3.
limitations: Only odd b>=7 and n=3 distinct-inversion rank; does not prove Conjecture 2.7 for n=4,5,6 or even b.
The sharp equality multipliers need coprimality; b=2 mod3 guarantees it.
